title: The alignment problem: whose values should AI follow?
kicker: Human feedback, hard choices and how to take part
blurb: How assistants learn behavior from human choices, four questions where reasonable people disagree, and the ways ordinary people can take part.
description: The film explains alignment as closing the gap between a capable model and one that is helpful, honest and harmless. It covers learning from human feedback and what went wrong when a model became flattering. It then walks through four open questions, the problem of whose values count, and concrete ways people can take part.
takeaways: A pretrained model is capable but does not know which of its possible answers people actually want, and alignment closes that gap.
The film describes a 2025 rollback of an overly flattering update, and draws the lesson that what we reward is what we get.
Medical advice, privacy, reporting users and whose side the model is on are dials that someone must set for every model.
The film argues that written values such as constitutions and specifications can be debated and improved, while hidden values cannot.
People can take part by voting, rating honestly, joining deliberations, reviewing tests in their own language and speaking up when rules are written.
